primary_rqs.question: Does the Software Behavior Genome remain stable under semantics-preserving transformations while being sensitive to semantics-changing transformations?

secondary_rqs.question: Does the structured 8-dimensional SBG outperform single-signal baselines in detecting behavioral regressions?
Which refactoring transformations are most/least challenging for SBG stability, and which genome dimensions drive the instability?
Can SBG identify semantically equivalent programs across programming languages using language-portable genome dimensions?
Can genome distance serve as a test-suite-free regression oracle, and does richer input sampling improve detection?
Does each of the 8 genome dimensions contribute independent, non-redundant behavioral signal across tasks?

exploratory_rqs.question: What is the minimum number of execution traces N* required for a reliable genome estimate, and how does it depend on program behavioral variance?
Do specific genome dimensions provide dominant signal for specific task categories?
Is genome distance monotonically increasing in syntactic change magnitude, and where does this break down?
What fraction of unrelated program pairs have genome distance below collision threshold epsilon_collision = 0.05?

hypotheses.name: Behavioral Genome Stability
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The mean behavioral distance between semantics-preserving program pairs equals the mean behavioral distance between semantics-changing pairs: E[D | equiv_S] = E[D | not-equiv_S].
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: E[D | semantics-preserving] << E[D | semantics-changing] with Cohen's d >= 0.8.
hypotheses.operationalization: Apply automated preserving (rename, extract, inline, dead-code, loop-hoist) and changing (Defects4J mutations) transforms to 50 programs. Compute D(G(P), G(P')) under I_prod with N=200 traces. Compare distributions with Mann-Whitney U.
hypotheses.statistical_test: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U; Bootstrap 95% CI on E[D_sp]; Cliff's delta
hypotheses.actual_sample_size: >=250 pairs per group (50 programs x 5 transforms)
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Mann-Whitney fails to reject H1_0 at alpha=0.0017, OR E[D_sp] > 0.10, OR more than 10% of preserving pairs have D > 0.05, OR Cliff's delta < 0.4.

hypotheses.name: Structured SBG Outperforms Baselines
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: There is no statistically significant difference in F1 score between the full 8-dimensional SBG and the best single-signal baseline on Defects4J.
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: SBG-8D achieves higher F1 and AUC-ROC than every evaluated baseline (code2vec, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, syntactic diff, single-dimension SBG).
hypotheses.operationalization: Compute D(G^k, G^{k+1}) for all Defects4J consecutive version pairs. Label as regression iff Defects4J marks bug-fix commit. Sweep theta 0->1. Report F1(theta*), AUC-ROC, AUC-PR on held-out test split.
hypotheses.statistical_test: DeLong's test for AUC comparison; McNemar's test for paired classification; Bootstrap 95% CI on delta-AUC
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Any baseline achieves F1 >= F1(SBG-8D) with statistical significance, OR DeLong test shows AUC(SBG) not > AUC(CodeBERT) at alpha=0.0017, OR SBG F1 < 0.70 on test split.

hypotheses.name: Robustness Under Refactoring
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Mean behavioral distance after refactoring equals mean behavioral distance after semantics-changing mutation: E[D | refactoring] = E[D | mutation].
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: E[D | refactoring] << E[D | mutation] for all 9 refactoring types, with Cohen's d >= 0.8.
hypotheses.operationalization: Apply 9 refactoring types × 3 magnitudes to 50 programs (1350 pairs). Compute D and d_k for each. Fit linear model D ~ type + magnitude + domain. Test stability per type with Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn post-hoc.
hypotheses.statistical_test: Kruskal-Wallis; Dunn post-hoc with Holm correction; paired Mann-Whitney (refactoring vs. mutation per type)
hypotheses.actual_sample_size: 150 per refactoring type (50 programs x 3 magnitudes)
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Any refactoring type yields E[D] > 0.10, OR more than 20% of any refactoring type's pairs exceed D=0.05, OR any type is indistinguishable from mutation at alpha=0.0017.

hypotheses.name: Cross-Language Generalization
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Behavioral distance between cross-language equivalent pairs is not significantly smaller than between random non-equivalent cross-language pairs.
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: D_portable(C_E(G(P_L1)), C_E(G(P_L2))) is significantly smaller for equivalent pairs, with Cliff's delta >= 0.5, restricted to dimensions {g_C, g_D, g_X}.
hypotheses.operationalization: For each of 5 algorithm classes × 5 language pairs: compute D_portable(G_L1, G_L2) for equivalent pairs and D_portable(G_L1, G_L2_other) for non-equivalent. Compare with Mann-Whitney U.
hypotheses.statistical_test: Mann-Whitney U; Linear mixed model (D ~ language_pair + algorithm_class with random effects); Bootstrap 95% CI on epsilon_xlang
hypotheses.actual_sample_size: >=35 equivalent pairs per language pair (augmented with RosettaCode implementations)
hypotheses.falsification_condition: E[D_equiv] > 0.20, OR Mann-Whitney fails at alpha=0.0017, OR 95% CI for E[D_equiv] entirely exceeds 0.15 on any language pair.

hypotheses.name: Genome as Regression Oracle
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: AUC-ROC(SBG) <= 0.70 on the held-out regression corpus at all thresholds theta.
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: AUC-ROC(SBG) > 0.80 AND there exists theta* with Recall(theta*) >= 0.80, Precision(theta*) >= 0.70 on the held-out Defects4J test split.
controls: theta* selected on validation split only
hypotheses.operationalization: Compute D(G^k, G^{k+1}) for all Defects4J version pairs. Sweep theta, find theta* = argmax F1 on validation. Evaluate Precision(theta*), Recall(theta*), AUC-ROC, AUC-PR on test split. Repeat under I_cov and I_adv.
hypotheses.expected_effect_direction: AUC-ROC rises above 0.80; Recall >= 0.80, Precision >= 0.70 at theta*
hypotheses.min_effect_size_unit: AUC-ROC points above H5_0 baseline of 0.70
hypotheses.statistical_test: DeLong's test (AUC vs baseline); Bootstrap 95% CI on AUC-ROC; McNemar test vs best baseline
hypotheses.falsification_condition: AUC-ROC < 0.80 on test split under any input distribution, OR no theta achieves Recall >= 0.80 AND Precision >= 0.70 simultaneously, OR F1 at theta* < 0.70.

hypotheses.name: Multi-Dimensional Value
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: For every task, a strict subset S with |S| <= 6 dimensions achieves the same performance as the full 8-dimensional SBG (no statistically significant difference in AUC-ROC).
hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: For at least one task, adding each of the 8 dimensions individually provides a statistically significant improvement over the 7-dimensional ablation that omits it (DELTA-AUC >= 0.03 per omitted dimension).
independent_variables: dimension_subset (all 256 subsets; focus on 8 leave-one-out and 8 single-dimension)
task (regression detection, clone detection, cross-language matching)
controls: uniform weights renormalized over included dimensions
same task evaluation protocol as H2 and H5
hypotheses.operationalization: For each of 8 leave-one-out ablations: compute AUC-ROC on 3 tasks. Compute per-dimension mutual information. Compute Pearson correlation matrix of {d_k}. Fit LASSO on task labels with cross-validated lambda.
hypotheses.expected_effect_direction: All 8 dimensions contribute non-redundant signal; each leave-one-out drops AUC by >= 0.03
hypotheses.expected_magnitude: Max |r(d_j, d_k)| < 0.50; LASSO selects >= 7 non-zero coefficients; DELTA-AUC >= 0.03 per omitted dimension
hypotheses.statistical_test: Friedman test (9 model variants); Nemenyi post-hoc with Holm correction; paired DeLong test (full vs each ablation); LASSO path analysis
hypotheses.actual_sample_size: 395+ version pairs (Defects4J); augmented by BigCloneBench and H4 corpus
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Any 6-dimension subset achieves equal AUC as 8D model (DeLong p > 0.0017) on all 3 tasks, OR LASSO selects <= 5 dimensions on any task, OR any two dimensions have |r| > 0.85.

sub_hypotheses.name: Dimension-Wise Stability Ordering
sub_hypotheses.informal: Under semantics-preserving transforms, dimensions follow a consistent stability ordering: CONTROL >= DATA >= INTERACTION > STATE > ERROR > RESOURCE > TEMPORAL > EXECUTION.
sub_hypotheses.operationalization: Extract per-dimension distances from H1/H3 experiments. Compute E[d_k]. Test ordering with one-sided Mann-Whitney between adjacent pairs.
sub_hypotheses.mechanistic_insight: Justifies FORMAL_MODEL.md caveat on TEMPORAL/RESOURCE; guides task-specific dimension selection.
sub_hypotheses.falsification: Any inversion of adjacent pair with |E[d_j] - E[d_k]| > 0.03.

sub_hypotheses.name: Input Coverage Governs Sensitivity
sub_hypotheses.informal: Recall(SBG, I_cov) > Recall(SBG, I_prod) > Recall(SBG, I_unif), especially for rare-trigger regressions.
sub_hypotheses.operationalization: Stratify Defects4J regressions by mu_prod(Delta) into rare/medium/common. Compare Recall under I_prod, I_unif, I_cov per stratum.
sub_hypotheses.mechanistic_insight: Directly tests the formal dependency of H2 on input coverage from FORMAL_MODEL.md. Motivates when to use coverage-guided inputs.

sub_hypotheses.name: Genome Convergence Rate
sub_hypotheses.informal: ||G_N - G_inf|| decreases as O(1/sqrt(N)), addressing Open Problem OP-1 from FORMAL_MODEL.md.
sub_hypotheses.operationalization: For N in {10,25,50,100,200,500,1000}: compute G_N and compare to G_10000 as reference. Fit log-log regression. Test H0: alpha = -0.5.
sub_hypotheses.mechanistic_insight: Establishes practical minimum N; if alpha ~ -0.5, N=200 gives reliable estimates.
sub_hypotheses.falsification: alpha > -0.3 (convergence slower than O(N^{-0.3})), implying N=1000 is insufficient for high-variance programs.

sub_hypotheses.name: Behavioral Distance is Locally Monotone in Code Change Size
sub_hypotheses.informal: D(G^k, G^{k+1}) is positively correlated with |Delta_code| in expectation across typical commits (tests FORMAL_MODEL.md H4).
sub_hypotheses.operationalization: Extract consecutive version pairs from 10 GitHub projects (>=100 commits). Compute Spearman rho(|Delta_code|, D). Stratify by commit type (refactoring / feature / bug fix).
sub_hypotheses.mechanistic_insight: Confirms O(|Delta_code|^alpha) claim; identifies alpha exponent and breakdown conditions.
sub_hypotheses.falsification: Median rho < 0.2 across projects, or rho < 0 on any project.

sub_hypotheses.name: Dimension-Task Specialization
sub_hypotheses.informal: g_C and g_D dominate for algorithm equivalence; g_E and g_R for performance regression; g_X and g_S for security analysis.
sub_hypotheses.operationalization: For 4 tasks (algorithm equivalence, performance regression, null-dereference detection, output regression): compute standalone AUC per dimension. Test if predicted dominant dimension is top-2 by Friedman test.
sub_hypotheses.mechanistic_insight: Justifies task-specific non-uniform weights w_k; guides practitioners on dimension selection per use case.
sub_hypotheses.falsification: No single dimension achieves AUC >= 0.65 standalone for any task, or predicted dominant dimension is not top-2 on any task.

prerequisite_order.rationale: Foundational: establishes N sufficiency before any other experiment
Core stability claim requires N to be validated first
Refactoring robustness specializes H1 to a defined transform class
Per-dimension data from H1 experiments required
Monotonicity test requires D to be validated as meaningful
Cross-language comparison requires N sufficiency and input protocol
Regression oracle recall depends on stability (H1) and input coverage (SH-2)
Baseline comparison meaningful only if SBG signal established
Multi-dimensional value analysis requires all dimension stability data

bonferroni_correction.note: All significance thresholds apply Bonferroni correction across H1-H6. Sub-hypotheses tested at alpha=0.01 (exploratory).

supplementary_corpora: Custom refactoring suite (50 programs x 9 types x 3 magnitudes, H3)
corpus_requirements.validation_protocol: 60/20/20 train/val/test split by project for Defects4J
